disease_label_per_paper: Perinephric abscess diagnosed by point-of-care ultrasound
presentation_summary: 87-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer, obstructive uropathy, prior right nephrostomy tube, and stage III CKD was transferred with gross hematuria and dysuria.
Two days before admission he had subjective fevers and generalized weakness; the outside hospital noted creatinine 5.6 mg/dL and urinalysis concerning for UTI.
At the receiving hospital, vital signs were within normal limits, abdomen was nontender, prior nephrostomy site appeared unremarkable, and Foley catheter drained clear yellow urine.
Initial labs showed WBC 28.2 x 10^3/uL, BUN 80 mg/dL, creatinine 4.85 mg/dL, and urinalysis with more than 100 WBC and RBC per high-power field plus a few yeast.
Renal POCUS showed a right perinephric anechoic fluid collection with no hydronephrosis; interventional radiology confirmed the perinephric collection.

imaging.finding: Reported right hydronephrosis and right upper-pole renal mass; source images were unavailable after transfer.
imaging.source_text_value: outside bedside renal ultrasound reportedly showed right sided hydronephrosis and a right upper pole renal mass

imaging.finding: Right perinephric anechoic fluid collection without hydronephrosis.
imaging.source_text_value: on the right, a perinephric anechoic fluid collection was seen, no hydronephrosis was present

microbiology.source_text_value: Blood cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida glabrata
The perinephric fluid collection grew Escherichia coli

microbiology.result: 4.2 mg/dL when serum creatinine was 4.3 mg/dL
microbiology.source_text_value: Creatinine from the fluid collection was 4.2 mg/dL (serum creatinine was 4.3 mg/dL)

procedures.source_text_value: IR injected contrast via the prior nephrostomy tube tract and contrast reached the perinephric fluid collection
A percutaneous drain was inserted into the fluid collection with return of about 30 mL purulent fluid

clinical_course.event: Repeat ultrasound showed resolution of the anechoic fluid collection after drainage.
Creatinine returned to baseline and the patient was discharged on fluconazole and cefepime; drain removed two weeks after discharge.

actual_treatment: percutaneous drainage of right perinephric collection

outcome.source_text_value: creatinine returned to baseline and patient was doing well at follow-up

quality_warnings: Organism identity, fluid creatinine, drainage result, and treatment response are retained but marked use_in_ranking=false.
The outside ultrasound renal-mass/hydronephrosis interpretation is preserved as a mimic context but not used as definitive ranking evidence.
Exact admission vital-sign numbers were not reported; normal vital signs are encoded only as an afebrile conservative body_temperature observation.
